questions.stem: Why did Lena write the email?

screens.title: The Three-Field System
text: For many centuries, farmers across much of Europe divided their land into two large fields. Each year, one field was planted with grain, while the other was deliberately left unplanted, or fallow, so that the soil could recover its natural fertility. This method protected the soil, but it meant that half of the available land produced nothing in any given year.

Around the eighth century, many villages began organizing their land into three fields instead. One field was sown with wheat or rye in the autumn, a second was planted in spring with oats, peas, or beans, and the third was allowed to rest. The crops then rotated to a different field each year.

This change brought two significant advantages. First, two-thirds of the land was now under cultivation at any time. Second, peas and beans naturally return nitrogen to the soil, so the fields remained productive for longer. The additional oats also supported more horses, which could plow considerably faster than oxen.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why European farmers stopped growing wheat and rye
A new way of farming that made fields more productive
How horses gradually replaced oxen on farms across Europe
Why fallow fields produced the largest harvests

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): the move from two fields to three and its advantages. C turns a minor detail into the main topic; A and D contradict the passage.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): iki tarladan üç tarlaya geçiş ve faydaları. C küçük bir ayrıntıyı ana konu yapıyor; A ve D metinle çelişiyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): el paso de dos campos a tres y sus ventajas. C convierte un detalle menor en el tema principal; A y D contradicen el texto.

questions.stem: The word "recover" in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: measure
protect
regain
remove

why.en: Vocabulary in context: the field rested so that the soil could "recover" (regain) its natural fertility. B borrows "protected" from the next sentence.
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: tarla, toprak doğal verimliliğini "recover" etsin (geri kazansın) diye dinlendiriliyordu. B sonraki cümledeki "protected" kelimesini ödünç alıyor.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: el campo descansaba para que la tierra pudiera "recover" (recuperar) su fertilidad natural. B toma prestado "protected" de la frase siguiente.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that "half of the available land produced nothing in any given year"?
options: To show a disadvantage of the two-field method
To show that European soil was too poor for grain
To explain why villages needed more horses
To argue that resting the soil was unnecessary

why.en: Author's purpose: the sentence shows the cost of the two-field system, which the three-field system later reduced. D goes too far, since one field still rested; C links the point to a later, unrelated detail.
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: cümle, iki tarla sisteminin bedelini gösteriyor; üç tarla sistemi bu bedeli sonradan azalttı. D aşırıya kaçıyor, çünkü bir tarla yine dinlendiriliyordu; C bu noktayı sonraki ilgisiz bir ayrıntıya bağlıyor.
why.es: Propósito del autor: la frase muestra el coste del sistema de dos campos, que el de tres campos redujo después. D va demasiado lejos, porque un campo seguía descansando; C relaciona la idea con un detalle posterior que no tiene que ver.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about villages that adopted the three-field system?
options: They no longer needed to leave any of their fields empty
They planted all of their crops in the spring
They gave up keeping oxen within a few years
They could grow more food on the same amount of land

why.en: Inference: two-thirds of the land was cultivated instead of half. A contradicts "the third was allowed to rest"; B ignores the autumn sowing of wheat or rye.
why.tr: Çıkarım: arazinin yarısı yerine üçte ikisi ekiliyordu. A "the third was allowed to rest" bilgisiyle çelişiyor; B buğday ya da çavdarın sonbaharda ekildiğini göz ardı ediyor.
why.es: Inferencia: se cultivaban dos tercios de la tierra en lugar de la mitad. A contradice "the third was allowed to rest"; B ignora la siembra de trigo o centeno en otoño.

questions.stem: According to the passage, why did the fields remain productive for longer?
options: Oats were planted in autumn instead of spring
Peas and beans returned nitrogen to the soil
Horses plowed the soil more deeply than oxen
The same crop grew in each field every year

why.en: Detail (close to the text): "peas and beans naturally return nitrogen to the soil". A reverses the seasons; C turns the point about plowing speed into a point about the soil.
why.tr: Ayrıntı (metne yakın): "peas and beans naturally return nitrogen to the soil". A mevsimleri tersine çeviriyor; C sürme hızıyla ilgili bilgiyi toprakla ilgili bir bilgiye dönüştürüyor.
why.es: Detalle (cercano al texto): "peas and beans naturally return nitrogen to the soil". A invierte las estaciones; C convierte lo dicho sobre la velocidad al arar en algo sobre la tierra.

hard.title: Updated Course Withdrawal Policy
text: Updated Course Withdrawal Policy

Beginning this fall, students may withdraw from a course through the student portal until the end of the tenth week of the semester; previously, the limit was the eighth week. Withdrawals made after the second week will appear on the transcript as a "W," which does not affect the grade point average. Students holding scholarships that require full-time enrollment should consult the Financial Aid Office before withdrawing, since dropping below twelve credits may reduce their award. A "W" on the transcript will now lower the grade point average

why.en: Main change (paraphrase): the deadline moves from the eighth to the tenth week. B mixes up the refund period with the withdrawal deadline; C contradicts "does not affect the grade point average".
why.tr: Ana değişiklik (parafraz): son tarih sekizinci haftadan onuncu haftaya kayıyor. B ücret iadesi süresini çekilme son tarihiyle karıştırıyor; C "does not affect the grade point average" bilgisiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Cambio principal (paráfrasis): el plazo pasa de la octava a la décima semana. B confunde el periodo de reembolso con el plazo para retirarse; C contradice "does not affect the grade point average".

questions.stem: What can be inferred about a student who withdraws from a course in the fourth week?
options: The course will not appear on the student's transcript
Not all of the money they paid will be returned
The student's grade point average will be lowered
The student must provide documents explaining the decision

why.en: Inference: full refunds are given only in the first two weeks, so a fourth-week withdrawal does not qualify. A applies only to very early withdrawals (a "W" appears after week two); D describes withdrawals after the tenth week.
why.tr: Çıkarım: tam iade yalnızca ilk iki haftada yapılıyor, dördüncü haftadaki çekilme bu kapsama girmiyor. A yalnızca çok erken çekilmeler için geçerli (ikinci haftadan sonra transkriptte "W" görünür); D onuncu haftadan sonraki çekilmeleri anlatıyor.
why.es: Inferencia: el reembolso completo solo se da en las dos primeras semanas, así que retirarse en la cuarta no da derecho a él. A solo vale para retiradas muy tempranas (tras la segunda semana aparece una "W"); D describe las retiradas después de la décima semana.

why.tr: Ayrıntı ("dropping below twelve credits may reduce their award" ifadesinin parafrazı). D yönü tersine çeviriyor (daha az yerine daha fazla kredi); A iki haftalık iade kuralını ödünç alıyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis de "dropping below twelve credits may reduce their award"). D invierte la dirección (más créditos en vez de menos); A toma prestada la regla del reembolso de dos semanas.

hard.title: The Strength of Weak Ties
hard.directions: Read an Academic Passage — upper module
text: Sociologists distinguish between strong ties, such as those connecting close friends and relatives, and weak ties, which link acquaintances who interact only occasionally. Intuitively, one might assume that strong ties constitute the more valuable resource, since close contacts are typically more willing to offer assistance.

A frequently cited study of professional workers, however, found that people who had obtained jobs through personal contacts more often heard about the position from acquaintances than from close friends. The explanation proposed was structural: members of a tightly knit circle tend to know the same people and encounter the same information, whereas acquaintances move in different social circles and can therefore transmit news that would otherwise remain inaccessible.

Subsequent research has qualified this conclusion. Strong ties appear more influential when information is scarce or when a recommendation requires considerable trust, and the advantage of weak ties seems to depend on the type of labor market. Nevertheless, the central insight, that the value of a connection lies partly in the novelty of what it can provide, has proved remarkably durable.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A finding about the value of distant contacts and later limits on it
How professional workers can turn their acquaintances into close friends
Why strong ties always outperform weak ties during a job search
The research methods that sociologists use to measure friendship

why.en: Main idea (paraphrase): the weak-ties finding, its explanation and the later qualifications. C contradicts the study; B invents a topic the passage never discusses.
why.tr: Ana fikir (parafraz): zayıf bağlar bulgusu, açıklaması ve sonradan getirilen sınırlamalar. C çalışmayla çelişiyor; B metinde hiç ele alınmayan bir konu uyduruyor.
why.es: Idea principal (paráfrasis): el hallazgo sobre los lazos débiles, su explicación y los matices posteriores. C contradice el estudio; B se inventa un tema que el texto nunca trata.

questions.stem: The word "qualified" in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: certified
confirmed
rejected
limited

why.en: Vocabulary in context: later research "qualified" the conclusion, i.e. limited it by adding conditions. A is another meaning of "qualified" that does not fit here; C is too strong, because the central insight survived.
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: sonraki araştırmalar sonucu "qualified" etti, yani koşullar ekleyerek sınırladı. A "qualified" kelimesinin buraya uymayan başka bir anlamı; C fazla güçlü, çünkü temel fikir geçerliliğini korudu.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: la investigación posterior "qualified" la conclusión, es decir, la limitó añadiendo condiciones. A es otro significado de "qualified" que aquí no encaja; C es demasiado fuerte, porque la idea central se mantuvo.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that members of a tightly knit circle "tend to know the same people"?
options: To argue that close friends are usually unwilling to help
To explain why close contacts often provide little new information
To show that the study included too few professional workers
To describe how acquaintances eventually become close friends

why.en: Author's purpose: it is part of the structural explanation, in which close friends share the same information while acquaintances bring news from other circles. A contradicts "more willing to offer assistance".
why.tr: Yazarın amacı: bu, yapısal açıklamanın parçası; yakın arkadaşlar aynı bilgiyi paylaşırken tanıdıklar başka çevrelerden haber getirir. A "more willing to offer assistance" bilgisiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Propósito del autor: forma parte de la explicación estructural: los amigos íntimos comparten la misma información, mientras que los conocidos traen noticias de otros círculos. A contradice "more willing to offer assistance".

questions.stem: Based on the passage, in which situation would a strong tie most likely be more useful than a weak one?
options: When news about job openings is easy to find
When a person wants news from unfamiliar social circles
When an employer wants a reliable personal reference
When acquaintances belong to many different groups

why.en: Inference: strong ties matter more "when a recommendation requires considerable trust". A is the opposite of "information is scarce"; B and D describe situations in which weak ties are the useful ones.
why.tr: Çıkarım: güçlü bağlar "when a recommendation requires considerable trust" durumunda daha etkili. A "information is scarce" ifadesinin tersi; B ve D zayıf bağların işe yaradığı durumları anlatıyor.
why.es: Inferencia: los lazos fuertes pesan más "when a recommendation requires considerable trust". A es lo contrario de "information is scarce"; B y D describen situaciones en las que son útiles los lazos débiles.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what did the study of professional workers find?
options: Job news came more often from acquaintances than from friends
Close friends were the most common source of job leads
Most workers found their jobs without help from any personal contacts
Acquaintances gave less reliable information than friends

why.en: Detail (paraphrase): people more often heard about the position "from acquaintances than from close friends". B reverses the finding; C contradicts "obtained jobs through personal contacts".
why.tr: Ayrıntı (parafraz): insanlar iş ilanını daha çok "from acquaintances than from close friends" duymuştu. B bulguyu tersine çeviriyor; C "obtained jobs through personal contacts" bilgisiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Detalle (paráfrasis): la gente se enteraba del puesto más a menudo "from acquaintances than from close friends". B invierte el hallazgo; C contradice "obtained jobs through personal contacts".

easy.title: Light in the Ocean
easy.directions: Read an Academic Passage — lower module
text: Sunlight does not go very deep into the ocean. Scientists divide the ocean into zones based on how much light reaches them. The top zone, down to about 200 meters, gets plenty of sunlight. Most sea plants and many fish live there.

Below that is the twilight zone. Only a little blue light reaches it, and plants cannot grow there. Deeper still, below 1,000 meters, the water is completely dark. Many animals in this deep zone make their own light. They use it to find food, to attract partners, or to confuse enemies.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why fish need blue light in order to grow
How scientists measure how deep the sea is
Why most sea plants live in shallow water close to the shore
How the amount of light changes with depth in the ocean

why.en: Main idea: the passage describes the ocean's zones by the light that reaches them. A and C are never discussed; B misreads "Scientists divide the ocean into zones".
why.tr: Ana fikir: metin okyanus katmanlarını aldıkları ışığa göre anlatıyor. A ve C metinde hiç geçmiyor; B "Scientists divide the ocean into zones" cümlesini yanlış okuyor.
why.es: Idea principal: el texto describe las zonas del océano según la luz que les llega. A y C no se tratan; B malinterpreta "Scientists divide the ocean into zones".

questions.stem: According to the passage, where do most sea plants live?
options: In the twilight zone of the ocean
In the water below 1,000 meters
In the top zone of the ocean
Next to deep-sea animals

why.en: Detail: "Most sea plants and many fish live there", in the top zone. A is the zone where "plants cannot grow".
why.tr: Ayrıntı: "Most sea plants and many fish live there", yani en üst katmanda. A "plants cannot grow" denen katman.
why.es: Detalle: "Most sea plants and many fish live there", es decir, en la zona superior. A es la zona donde "plants cannot grow".

questions.stem: The word "plenty" in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: a small amount
a large amount
a certain color
a short time

why.en: Vocabulary in context: the top zone "gets plenty of sunlight" = a large amount. A is the opposite meaning.
why.tr: Bağlamda kelime: en üst katman "gets plenty of sunlight" = bol miktarda alıyor. A tam tersi anlam.
why.es: Vocabulario en contexto: la zona superior "gets plenty of sunlight" = recibe mucha luz. A significa lo contrario.

questions.stem: Why can't plants grow in the twilight zone?
options: There is not enough light for them
The water there is completely dark
The animals there eat all of them
The water there is far too salty

why.en: Inference: only "a little blue light" reaches this zone, so plants lack the light they need. B describes the zone below 1,000 meters, not the twilight zone.

screens.title: Academic Talk: From harpsichord to piano
screens.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in a music history class.

audio.text: Today I want to look at an instrument you all know, the piano, and why it was such an important change. Before about 1700, the main keyboard instrument in Europe was the harpsichord. When you press a key on a harpsichord, a small quill called a plectrum plucks the string. The problem is that the plectrum plucks it in the same way no matter how hard you press, so a player can't make one note louder than another.

Around 1700, an instrument maker in Florence, Bartolomeo Cristofori, replaced the plectrum with a small hammer that strikes the string and then falls away. Press the key gently and the hammer hits softly; press it hard and the note is loud. That's where the name comes from: pianoforte means soft-loud in Italian.

Interestingly, the new instrument didn't catch on right away. Early pianos were quiet and expensive, and many musicians saw no reason to give up the harpsichord. It took several decades before composers began writing music that depended on gradual changes in volume. Then, in the nineteenth century, builders added iron frames, which could hold thicker strings under much greater tension. Pianos became loud enough to fill large concert halls, and that's the instrument we recognize today.

questions.stem: What is the lecture mainly about?
options: The development of a keyboard that could play softly or loudly
Why many performers today still prefer the harpsichord to the piano
How concert halls in Florence were designed for music
The life and work of a famous composer of the 1700s

why.en: Main idea: how the piano solved the harpsichord's volume problem and later grew louder. B reverses the direction of the lecture; C misuses "Florence", where the inventor worked.
why.tr: Ana fikir: piyanonun klavsenin ses şiddeti sorununu nasıl çözdüğü ve sonra nasıl daha güçlü hâle geldiği. B dersin yönünü tersine çeviriyor; C mucidin çalıştığı yer olan "Florence" kelimesini yanlış kullanıyor.
why.es: Idea principal: cómo el piano resolvió el problema de volumen del clavecín y después ganó potencia. B invierte el sentido de la clase; C usa mal "Florence", donde trabajaba el inventor.

questions.stem: According to the professor, what was the main limitation of the harpsichord?
options: Its strings often broke when the keys were pressed hard
It was much too loud for small rooms in private homes

Its hammers fell away from the strings too quickly

why.en: Detail: the plectrum plucks the string "in the same way no matter how hard you press". D gives the harpsichord the piano's hammers; A is never mentioned.
why.tr: Ayrıntı: kanca teli "in the same way no matter how hard you press" çekiyor. D piyanonun çekiçlerini klavsene mal ediyor; A hiç söylenmiyor.
why.es: Detalle: el gancho pulsa la cuerda "in the same way no matter how hard you press". D atribuye al clavecín los martillos del piano; A nunca se menciona.

questions.stem: Why does the professor explain the meaning of the word "pianoforte"?
options: To prove that the piano was invented by an Italian composer
To explain why early pianos were so expensive to build
To introduce a second instrument made in Florence
To show that the name describes what the instrument could do

why.en: Purpose: "soft-loud" names exactly the new ability to vary the volume. A turns the instrument maker into a composer; B links the name to a different point.
why.tr: Amaç: "soft-loud", ses şiddetini değiştirme yeteneğini tam olarak adlandırıyor. A çalgı yapımcısını besteciye dönüştürüyor; B adı başka bir noktaya bağlıyor.
why.es: Propósito: "soft-loud" nombra justo la nueva capacidad de variar el volumen. A convierte al fabricante de instrumentos en compositor; B relaciona el nombre con otro punto.

questions.stem: What does the professor imply about nineteenth-century pianos?
options: They cost much less to build than the earliest pianos did
They could be heard clearly in big performance spaces
They went back to using plectrums instead of hammers
They were played mostly in small private homes

why.en: Inference from "loud enough to fill large concert halls". D contradicts that point; C reverses the history of the mechanism.
why.tr: "Loud enough to fill large concert halls" ifadesinden çıkarım. D bununla çelişiyor; C mekanizmanın tarihini tersine çeviriyor.
why.es: Inferencia a partir de "loud enough to fill large concert halls". D contradice esa idea; C invierte la historia del mecanismo.

hard.title: Academic Talk: How migrating birds find their way
hard.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.

audio.text: Every autumn, millions of songbirds fly thousands of kilometers to their wintering grounds, and many of them travel at night, alone, on their very first journey. So how do they know which way to go? It turns out they don't rely on a single cue. They carry what amounts to several compasses.

One is the sun. Birds that fly by day can judge direction from the sun's position, adjusting for the time of day. Night migrants need something else, and a classic experiment revealed what it was. Researchers raised young birds in a planetarium, under an artificial sky that rotated around a different star than the real North Star. When migration season arrived, the birds oriented themselves using that false center of rotation. In other words, they had learned the pattern of the sky; they hadn't inherited a map of particular stars.

Birds also sense the Earth's magnetic field. Interestingly, their magnetic compass doesn't distinguish north from south the way ours does. Instead, it detects the angle at which the field lines dip toward the ground, which tells a bird whether it's heading toward the pole or toward the equator. And on overcast nights, when the stars disappear, that magnetic sense appears to keep them on course.

why.en: Main idea: birds use several "compasses" (the sun, the stars, the magnetic field). D contradicts "alone, on their very first journey"; C turns the setting of the experiment into the topic.
why.tr: Ana fikir: kuşlar birkaç "pusula" kullanır (güneş, yıldızlar, manyetik alan). D "alone, on their very first journey" ile çelişiyor; C deneyin yapıldığı yeri konu hâline getiriyor.
why.es: Idea principal: las aves usan varias "brújulas" (el sol, las estrellas, el campo magnético). D contradice "alone, on their very first journey"; C convierte el lugar del experimento en el tema.

hard.title: Academic Talk: Finding planets around other stars
hard.prompt: Listen to part of a lecture in an astronomy class.

audio.text: Planets orbiting other stars are extremely hard to see directly. A star is billions of times brighter than any planet near it, so the planet's faint light is simply lost in the glare. Instead, astronomers usually detect these planets indirectly, and today the most productive approach is called the transit method.

Here's the idea. If a planet's orbit happens to be lined up with our line of sight, then once per orbit the planet passes in front of its star. When that happens, it blocks a tiny fraction of the starlight, often less than one percent. A sensitive telescope that measures the star's brightness continuously will record a small, regular dip. The time between dips tells us the length of the planet's year, and the depth of each dip tells us how large the planet is compared with its star.

Now, a single dip doesn't prove anything. Stars have dark spots, and a second star passing in front can produce a similar signal. That's why astronomers want to see at least three evenly spaced dips before they take a candidate seriously. And keep in mind the method's built-in bias: it only finds systems whose orbits we happen to see edge-on, so for every planet detected this way, many more must be passing by unseen.

questions.stem: What is the lecture mainly about?
options: Why some stars shine much more brightly than others
How telescopes take direct photographs of distant planets

why.en: Main idea: the transit method, its logic and its limits. B contradicts the opening point that such planets are "extremely hard to see directly".
why.tr: Ana fikir: geçiş yöntemi, mantığı ve sınırları. B bu gezegenlerin "extremely hard to see directly" olduğu yönündeki açılış bilgisiyle çelişiyor.
why.es: Idea principal: el método de tránsito, su lógica y sus límites. B contradice la idea inicial de que estos planetas son "extremely hard to see directly".

why.tr: Ayrıntı: "the depth of each dip tells us how large the planet is compared with its star". B düşüşler arasındaki sürenin gösterdiği şey; klasik yer değiştirme tuzağı.
why.es: Detalle: "the depth of each dip tells us how large the planet is compared with its star". B es lo que indica el tiempo entre caídas: la trampa clásica del intercambio.

why.tr: Amaç: lekeler, tıpkı ikinci bir yıldız gibi, düşüşü taklit edebilir; bu yüzden "a single dip doesn't prove anything". C rollerini tersine çeviriyor, çünkü lekeler yanıltıcı sinyal kaynağı.

why.tr: "For every planet detected this way, many more must be passing by unseen" ifadesinden çıkarım. C dersin girişiyle çelişiyor; A yalnızca gezegen sinyalini taklit edebilen karanlık lekelerle ilgili bilgiyi yanlış kullanıyor.
why.es: Inferencia a partir de "for every planet detected this way, many more must be passing by unseen". C contradice el inicio de la clase; A usa mal lo dicho sobre las manchas oscuras, que solo pueden imitar la señal de un planeta.

screens.prompt: Your professor is teaching a class on education. Write a post responding to the professor's question. Express and support your opinion, and make a contribution to the discussion in your own words.

professor.name: Okafor
professor.post: Many universities are debating whether every lecture should be recorded and posted online. Supporters say recordings help students review difficult material and help those who sometimes have to miss class because of work or family responsibilities. Others worry that if recordings are always available, fewer students will come to class, and discussions in the room will suffer. Should universities require professors to record all of their lectures? Why or why not?

students.name: Lucia
students.post: Yes, I think they should. Before my chemistry exam, I watched two lectures again, and parts I had missed the first time finally made sense. Also, many students have long commutes or part-time jobs. With a recording, missing one bus doesn't mean missing the material.

students.name: Tomas
students.post: I don't think it should be required. When my statistics professor started posting recordings, attendance dropped by almost half, and the few students who came rarely asked questions. Some professors also feel uncomfortable being recorded. Each professor should decide what works for their own course.
